after.title: Dead 12V Battery from Gateway or BECM Software Conditions
after.description: GM bulletin 23-NA-124 covers a dead 12V battery, no-start, inoperative passive-key functions and parasitic draw on the 2023 Lyriq when a Serial Data Gateway Module software anomaly keeps activity alive. after.solution: Have an EV-qualified Cadillac technician reproduce the draw and scan every module. For the 2023 gateway condition, cycle the specified fuse and verify or update the gateway software. Do not disconnect the 12V or high-voltage system from this card.

after.title: False ABS Activation Can Reduce Braking Below 25 mph (Recall 24V589)
after.description: Certain 2023-2024 Lyriq all-wheel-drive vehicles can falsely detect wheel slip on dry pavement below 25 mph. Under a specific wheel-movement sequence, ABS can continue releasing service-brake pressure and reduce or remove normal braking performance.
after.solution: Check the VIN and open-field-action status. Cadillac updates the Electronic Brake Control Module software over the air or at an authorized dealer under recall 24V589 / GM N242453471 at no charge. Do not assume a rear-wheel-drive Lyriq is included.
symptoms: Unexpected ABS activation on dry pavement below 25 mph

evidence.label: GM Preliminary Information PIC6586 - Charge Port Door Does Not Auto Close

after.title: Charge Port Door May Not Auto-Close After Unplugging
after.description: PIC6586 states that the 2023-2025 Lyriq charge-port door may remain open after the charging plug is removed because automatic closing was intentionally disabled to keep the dust cover from catching and breaking the door. This is a feature behavior, not proof of a failed door motor or charging module.
after.solution: No repair is required for this exact condition. Close the door with its button, or it will close automatically when the vehicle is shifted out of Park. If the door will not respond to either action or charging itself fails, have Cadillac diagnose that separate symptom.
symptoms: Charge port door remains open after unplugging

after.title: Loose Stabilizer Bracket Bolts Can Damage EV Cables (Recall 25V232)
after.description: On 17 identified 2023-2025 Lyriqs, improperly fastened left or right front stabilizer-bar bracket bolts can loosen and separate. A loose bar or bracket can damage high-voltage cables or battery-coolant lines, eventually making the vehicle shut off or become undriveable.
after.solution: Check the VIN for recall 25V232 / GM N252494190. An authorized Cadillac EV dealer inspects and, as necessary, properly fastens the affected bracket bolts at no charge. A clunk or rattle may precede separation; do not work near high-voltage cables from this card.
symptoms: Vehicle may shut off if adjacent EV systems are damaged
